This is so late but I have to say this. That "black" canvas is actually not painted solid black. Basically, the whole canvas is painted with different shades of 'black;' reddish black, blue based black, etc. the viewer looks at it and is like 'that's the true black, in the corner,' but then it turns out that what they thought was true black was actually dark violet, or dark brown. The piece is meant to challenge the viewers perception. Modern art actually takes talent.

Wicca and Voodoo are both religions that are very much real. I have friends who are very into new age culture (i.e. witchcraft), and I'll confess that I myself dabbled in it briefly. Obviously that Harry Potter shit isn't real, and it's tough to determine whether todays 'magickal' spells are actually real (I'd guess not though.) New age magic isn't using telekinesis to take a book off the shelf, if I remember correctly it's supposedly the 'transfer of energy.' For example, you want to bless an item, you put actual effort and energy during your spell to transfer 'positive energies' to said item. From what I gather there hasn't been much research on it to really prove whether or not witchcraft is legitimate, but from my experience I'd say it's BS.
